title: Topic 6 · العولمة والاندماج الثقافي (Globalisation and Cultural Assimilation)
blocks: h2
الـ Academic noun (10 كلمات)
ul
**globalisation** (العولمة): Globalisation has linked distant economies more closely than ever.
**assimilation** (الاندماج / الذوبان الثقافي): The assimilation of immigrants raises questions about cultural identity.
**homogenisation** (التجانس / التنميط): Critics warn of the homogenisation of world cultures.
**diversity** (التنوّع): Cultural diversity enriches modern cities.
**heritage** (التراث): Migration can dilute a community’s cultural heritage.
**identity** (الهوية): Young people often struggle to protect their national identity abroad.
**multiculturalism** (التعددية الثقافية): Multiculturalism has become a defining feature of large cities.
**interdependence** (الاعتماد المتبادل): Global interdependence makes isolation almost impossible.
**migration** (الهجرة): Mass migration reshapes both host and home countries.
**westernisation** (التغريب): Rapid westernisation worries many traditional societies.
h2
أفعال (verb) ذات معنى دقيق (10 أفعال) · صيغ past و participle و -ing
ul
**integrate** (integrated, integrated, integrating): Immigrants who integrate quickly tend to prosper.
**assimilate** (assimilated, assimilated, assimilating): Some minorities are pressured to assimilate into the majority culture.
**adapt** (adapted, adapted, adapting): Newcomers must adapt to unfamiliar customs.
**preserve** (preserved, preserved, preserving): Diaspora communities work hard to preserve their traditions.
**erode** (eroded, eroded, eroding): Foreign media can slowly erode local values.
**embrace** (embraced, embraced, embracing): Younger generations tend to embrace global culture.
**exchange** (exchanged, exchanged, exchanging): Nations exchange ideas as freely as goods.
**dominate** (dominated, dominated, dominating): A handful of languages dominate the internet.
**dilute** (diluted, diluted, diluting): Globalisation may dilute distinctive local customs.
**migrate** (migrated, migrated, migrating): Millions migrate each year in search of work.
h2
الـ Collocation والـ adjective (10 عبارات)
ul
**cultural diversity**: Cultural diversity is one of the strengths of a global city. (Writing)
**global marketplace**: Small firms can now reach the global marketplace. (Writing)
**cross-cultural**: Cross-cultural understanding reduces conflict. (Speaking and Writing)
**loss of identity**: Rapid change can lead to a loss of identity. (Writing)
**cultural exchange**: Tourism promotes valuable cultural exchange. (Writing)
**multinational corporations**: Multinational corporations shape global consumer habits. (Writing)
**deep-rooted traditions**: Some deep-rooted traditions resist outside influence. (Writing)
**global village**: The internet has turned the world into a global village. (Speaking and Writing)
**Western influence**: Western influence is visible in food, fashion, and film. (Writing)
**increasingly interconnected**: Economies are increasingly interconnected. (Writing)
h2
الـ formal collocation في Task 2 (5 عبارات) · للـ Writing
ul
**break down cultural barriers**: International education helps break down cultural barriers.
**at the risk of losing**: Nations modernise at the risk of losing their heritage.
**a sense of belonging**: A shared culture gives people a sense of belonging.
**erode traditional values**: Global media can erode traditional values.
**foster mutual understanding**: Cultural exchange fosters mutual understanding between nations.
h2
الـ idiom والـ expression في Speaking (5 عبارات) · للاستخدام في Speaking فقط
ul
**when in Rome**: I try to respect local customs, since when in Rome, you do as the Romans do. (Part 3)
**a melting pot**: My city is a real melting pot of cultures. (Part 3)
**feel at home**: Despite the differences, I quickly felt at home there. (Part 2)
**worlds apart**: The two cultures are worlds apart in some ways. (Part 3)
**bridge the gap**: Learning a language helps bridge the gap between cultures. (Part 3)

items.prompt: Has globalisation been mostly positive or negative for your country?
items.answer: Globalisation has been a mixed blessing: it has connected us to a global marketplace and fostered mutual understanding, yet it also risks eroding traditional values, so the world can feel both closer together and worlds apart.

items.prompt: Do you think local cultures are disappearing because of globalisation?

items.prompt: Do you think money is the most important measure of success?
items.answer: Money matters, but it is not the only measure of success; a person who climbs the career ladder while struggling to make ends meet may be far less content than someone with modest means and a fulfilling life.

items.prompt: Should governments do more to reduce the gap between rich and poor?
items.answer: Yes, I think so; unregulated markets tend to widen the gap between rich and poor, so governments should invest in public services and use fair taxation to support those struggling to make ends meet.

items.prompt: Is it better to work for a company or to be self-employed?
items.answer: It depends on the person; working for a company offers stability, whereas being self-employed offers freedom, so it is really about which side of that trade-off suits you.

blocks.instructions: أجب عن كل سؤال من أسئلة Part 3 في 2–3 جمل. استخدم في إجابتك 1 target idiom على الأقل و1 collocation على الأقل. ثم قارن إجابتك بالـ model answer.

items.prompt: Why is it important to protect traditional culture?
items.answer: Protecting traditional culture matters because it instils a sense of identity and offers a window into the past; customs that stand the test of time connect each generation to the one before it.

items.prompt: Do you think modern life is making traditions disappear?
items.answer: To a certain extent, yes; the fast pace of modern life pushes some customs aside, but renewed interest in heritage means many traditions still stand the test of time.

items.prompt: Should governments spend public money on the arts?
items.answer: I believe they should; public funding sustains the arts, which are an integral part of a nation’s identity and offer a window into its history that the market alone would not preserve.

title: Topic 10 · الإعلام والاتصال الجماهيري والإعلان (Media, Mass Communication and Advertising)
blocks: h2
الـ Academic noun (10 كلمات)
ul
**propaganda** (الدعاية الموجَّهة): Wartime propaganda shaped public feeling.
**censorship** (الرقابة): Media censorship limits what citizens can know.
**journalism** (الصحافة): Independent journalism holds power to account.
**bias** (التحيّز): Political bias can distort the news.
**consumerism** (النزعة الاستهلاكية): Advertising fuels a culture of consumerism.
**sensationalism** (الإثارة الإعلامية): Sensationalism sells papers but misleads readers.
**audience** (الجمهور): Advertisers tailor messages to a target audience.
**misinformation** (المعلومات الخاطئة): Misinformation spreads rapidly on social media.
**endorsement** (التأييد / الترويج): A celebrity endorsement can boost sales overnight.
**coverage** (التغطية الإعلامية): The event received worldwide coverage.
h2
أفعال (verb) ذات معنى دقيق (10 أفعال) · صيغ past و participle و -ing
ul
**broadcast** (broadcast, broadcast, broadcasting): The match was broadcast live worldwide.
**manipulate** (manipulated, manipulated, manipulating): Advertisers manipulate our emotions.
**advertise** (advertised, advertised, advertising): Companies advertise heavily during major events.
**influence** (influenced, influenced, influencing): The media strongly influences public opinion.
**endorse** (endorsed, endorsed, endorsing): Athletes endorse products for large fees.
**censor** (censored, censored, censoring): Some governments censor critical reporting.
**exaggerate** (exaggerated, exaggerated, exaggerating): Headlines often exaggerate the facts.
**promote** (promoted, promoted, promoting): Influencers promote brands to their followers.
**distort** (distorted, distorted, distorting): Selective editing can distort a story.
**inform** (informed, informed, informing): A free press informs and educates the public.
h2
الـ Collocation والـ adjective (10 عبارات)
ul
**mass media**: The mass media shapes how we see the world. (Writing)

**misleading advertising**: Misleading advertising should be regulated. (Writing)

**social media**: Social media has changed political campaigning. (Speaking and Writing)
**breaking news**: Breaking news now travels in seconds. (Speaking)
**biased reporting**: Biased reporting undermines public trust. (Writing)
**eye-catching**: An eye-catching advert grabs attention instantly. (Speaking and Writing)
**celebrity endorsement**: Celebrity endorsement drives youth spending. (Writing)

items.prompt: Do you think advertising has too much influence on people?
items.answer: Advertising certainly has too much influence, since clever campaigns manipulate consumer behaviour and encourage people to jump on the bandwagon of every trend, though a discerning viewer learns to take such messages with a pinch of salt.

items.prompt: Can we still trust the news we read online?
items.answer: Not entirely; much online content is biased or sensationalised, and misinformation spreads like wildfire, so it is wise to take what you read with a pinch of salt and check reliable sources.

items.prompt: How has social media changed the way people get information?
items.answer: Social media has transformed how we get information, since breaking news now travels in seconds; the downside is that it also lets rumours spread unchecked.
